answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a small stake in a shared vault before it can transact; the stake is slashed on proven misbehavior, so spawning many fake identities becomes expensive. Reputation is then grown slowly, like a cedar maturing over seasons, through verified work rather than self-declared claims. Finally, identities that pass repeated independent audits earn a forge mark, a tamper-evident credential binding their history to the stake, so cheap clones cannot inherit the trust of the original.
